_comment_purpose: Example .claude/settings.json — a starting point. Each template ships its own tailored copy; this is the default an application template adapts from. See templates/application/PERMISSIONS.md for the rationale behind each entry. Three layers: (1) allow = day-to-day autonomy (gh, uv, python, pytest, feature-branch git, jq, duckdb, sqlite3); (2) ask = anything that mutates a remote or destroys local state; (3) deny = anything outside the project root, anything destructive to main, and PR merging (you merge manually in the GitHub UI so the human stays in the loop). The end-of-session flow lives in templates/_shared/git-workflow.md.
_comment_hooks: The PreToolUse hook below is the runtime half of the no-cat-head-via-bash module (the H2 re-read guard): it blocks a redundant re-read of a file already read and unmodified this session. It's guarded with a `[ -f ] || exit 0` test, so it's a safe no-op until you vendor that module (which ships pre_read_guard.py) — delete the hook block if you don't want it. The module is the Read-tool half; the prose rule is the Bash-cat half, which is why `cat`/`head`/`tail` stay in the allow list (cat-of-command-output is a legitimate exception, so it's a behavioral rule, not a deny). Disable the guard for one session with H2_REREAD_GUARD_DISABLED=1. Other hook ideas (e.g. a PreToolUse hook that reminds 'backup before migration' on schema-changing SQL) belong here too — see templates/application/PERMISSIONS.md.
_comment_stop: The Stop hook below is the runtime half of the git-flow-session-end module: it nudges the agent back onto the session-end loop when it tries to end a turn with a MERGED PR un-cleaned-up or a clean+pushed OPEN PR at the hand-off point (the #1 dropped step — ending in prose instead of popping the AskUserQuestion merge popup). Same `[ -f ] || exit 0` guard, so it's a safe no-op until you vendor that module (which ships session_end_guard.py). It fails open and honors stop_hook_active, so it can never loop or wedge a session. Disable for one session with SESSION_END_GUARD_DISABLED=1. Delete the block if your repo doesn't follow GitHub Flow.
_comment_sessionstart: The SessionStart hook below is the runtime half of the session-handoff module: it surfaces a committed .claude/next-session.md (the roadmap-grounded kickoff the previous session wrote) into the new session's opening context, so the *read* side of the handoff is mechanical rather than agent-honored. Same `[ -f ] || exit 0` guard, so it's a safe no-op until you vendor that module (which ships session_handoff_kickoff.py); the script also no-ops when no next-session.md exists and FAILS OPEN on any error, so it can never wedge a session. Disable for one session with SESSION_HANDOFF_KICKOFF_DISABLED=1. Delete the block if you don't want the handoff auto-surfaced.
